recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Follow-up core source work is only needed if the work group wants a new normative-strength change from "needs" to "must".
issue_request: FHIR-18354 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core request to revise the Extensibility page's explanation of what it means to understand a modifier extension, clarifying that special handling code is not always required if the developer determines the modifier has no computational impact and reassesses as behavior changes.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 777cc3bf72adffe5bcab147da93d662ae4e804b9, titled "GF#18354 - fix language", which changed source/extensibility.html to add the computational-impact and repeat-assessment wording.
additional_context: source/extensibility.html is in current build scope via source/hierarchy.xml and source/navigation.xml. Focused Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting later discussion or minutes. The current source says the assessment "needs to be repeated" rather than the Jira description's proposed "must be repeated", but this preserves the substantive clarification without needing a new source change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active source already states that understanding a modifier extension can mean either providing handling instructions or determining the modifier does not impact the system's computational functions, and already says the assessment needs to be repeated when computational behavior changes.
